meta.description: Literal questions visitors ask, with short direct answers.

entries.title: Is Avrodeep open to new roles?
entries.question: Is Avrodeep open to new job opportunities?
entries.text: Not right now. He's committed to his role at GenAIus Technology and focused on that plus his research work and GATE 2028 preparation. He isn't looking at other opportunities at the moment.
aliases: is he looking for a job

entries.title: Does Avrodeep do freelance work?
entries.question: Does Avrodeep take freelance or consulting work?
entries.text: No. He doesn't do freelance. His time outside work goes to his research project and GATE preparation.
aliases: is he available for contract work
can I hire him for a project

entries.title: Can I collaborate with Avrodeep?
entries.question: Can I collaborate with Avrodeep on research or a project?
entries.text: Research conversations, yes — especially anything on reasoning models, RL post-training, or LLM security. He's not taking on build work or freelance projects. LinkedIn with a short note about the problem works best.

entries.title: How do I contact Avrodeep?
entries.question: How do I get in touch with Avrodeep?
entries.text: Through the Contact Me section on this site, or LinkedIn at linkedin.com/in/AvrodeepPal. He responds faster to specific messages than to generic introductions.

entries.title: Where is Avrodeep based?
entries.question: Where does Avrodeep live?
entries.text: Barrackpore, North 24 Parganas, in the Kolkata metropolitan area of West Bengal, India. He works remotely and commutes into Kolkata when needed.

entries.title: What does Avrodeep specialise in?
entries.question: What areas does Avrodeep specialise in?
entries.text: Professionally: LLM infrastructure — RAG pipelines, vector search, model serving, agent workflows, and the security hardening that keeps production AI systems standing. In research: reasoning in language models, specifically the trade-off between training-time and inference-time compute. Cybersecurity runs through both.

entries.title: Is Avrodeep preparing for GATE?
entries.question: Is Avrodeep preparing for GATE or higher studies?
entries.text: Yes — GATE 2028 is his main target. He sat it in 2024 and 2025 as practice and skipped 2026 for industry experience. The goal afterwards is an MS(Research) or research assistant position at an Indian AI lab working on reasoning models.

entries.title: Does Avrodeep want to do a PhD?
entries.question: Is Avrodeep planning a PhD?
entries.text: Possibly, but not immediately. The near-term plan is an MS(Research) or research assistant position after GATE 2028, which will tell him whether full-time research is the right fit before committing several years to a PhD.

entries.title: Does Avrodeep have publications?
entries.question: Does Avrodeep have research publications?
entries.text: Not in peer-reviewed venues yet. His MCA thesis on cross-lingual Bengali idiom matching is public on GitHub with full methodology and metrics — it produced an honest negative result. His current side project on reasoning models is working toward a first proper write-up.

entries.title: Where is Avrodeep's resume?
entries.question: Where can I find Avrodeep's resume or CV?
entries.text: It's linked from the home page of this portfolio. For a version tailored to a specific role, reach out through the Contact Me section.

entries.title: What is GenAIus Technology?
entries.question: What does GenAIus Technology do?
entries.text: A startup building an AI operating system — a platform where technical and non-technical users compose AI workflows as graphs of nodes, with models runnable on hardware you control. Avrodeep works on backend infrastructure, the workflow platform, security hardening and multimodal model integration.

entries.title: How much experience does Avrodeep have?
entries.question: How many years of experience does Avrodeep have?
entries.text: He's been at GenAIus Technology since January 2026 — first as a Python Developer Intern, then full-time from July 2026. Before that, his ML and software work was through academic projects and independent repos going back to 2021.

entries.title: What's Avrodeep's preferred stack?
entries.question: What tech stack does Avrodeep prefer?
entries.text: Python with FastAPI for services, PostgreSQL and Redis for storage, Docker for packaging. PyTorch with HuggingFace Transformers for ML. React and Tailwind on the frontend. Linux throughout. Java is his oldest language and still the one he'd pick for something built to last.

entries.title: What languages does Avrodeep speak?
entries.question: What human languages does Avrodeep speak?
entries.text: English, Bengali and Hindi. English is his working language; Bengali is his mother tongue.

entries.title: Would Avrodeep relocate?
entries.question: Is Avrodeep willing to relocate?
entries.text: He's not looking at roles right now. Longer term, for a research position he'd consider relocating — he chose a remote role earlier partly for family proximity, but that isn't a permanent constraint.

entries.title: Will Avrodeep help students?
entries.question: Will Avrodeep do mentoring or give advice to students?
entries.text: Occasionally, if the ask is specific. He was a placement coordinator at JU MCA so he's done a lot of it. If you're stuck on something concrete — ML, backend, LLM systems, security, or DSA — reach out on LinkedIn with the actual problem.

entries.title: What's Avrodeep's DSA background?
entries.question: What's Avrodeep's LeetCode or DSA level?
entries.text: He practises on LeetCode at leetcode.com/AvrodeepPal, mainly in C++ with the STL, currently as part of GATE 2028 preparation. He hasn't competed seriously on Codeforces yet. If you have good DSA practice advice, he'd like to hear it.

entries.title: How does this chatbot work?
entries.question: How was this chatbot built?
entries.text: It's a RAG pipeline. Avrodeep's background is written as structured entries, embedded into a vector store, and your question retrieves the closest matches which a language model then answers from. It's built to say it doesn't know rather than invent an answer — so if it declines, that's working as intended.
